name: Srinivasa Perumal Temple, Egmore
significance: A Vishnu temple in the Egmore quarter of Chennai, formerly called the Lakshmi Narayana Perumal temple, with a three-tiered gopuram and an Anantha Vimanam over the sanctum; it is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Sages including Visvamitra and Gautama are said to have worshipped at this spot.

name: Ezhava Siva, Aruvippuram
significance: The Shiva installed at Aruvippuram in 1888 by the social reformer Sree Narayana Guru, who as a non-Brahmin of the Ezhava community was challenged over his right to consecrate a temple and answered that he had installed an 'Ezhava Siva'. The act became a landmark in Kerala's fight against caste exclusion from temples, and the Guru inscribed there his vision of a place where all live in brotherhood regardless of caste or religion.

name: Shree Dwadasha Jyotirlinga Temple
deity: Omkareshwara (Shiva), with replicas of the twelve Jyotirlingas
style: Mixed South Indian and North Indian
significance: A modern Shaiva complex on Omkar Hills in Bengaluru, begun in 2002 under Sri Shivapuri Mahaswamiji and consecrated in February 2011, that gathers shrines representing all twelve Jyotirlingas in one place so pilgrims can circuit them without travelling across India.

name: Tapkeshwari Temple
significance: A goddess shrine set in a valley of the Tapkeshwari hill range south of Bhuj in Kachchh, a cave-riddled range noted for its indigenous plant and animal life.

name: Vadakkan Koyikkal Devi Temple, Puthiyavila
significance: A Devi temple near Kayamkulam whose unusual two-storey sreekovil places the goddess on the ground floor and Shiva above; Bhadrakali and Ayyappan are also worshipped here, and the ten-day Kumbha Bharani with its kettukazhcha displays is the principal festival.

name: Thandu Mariamman Temple
significance: A Mariamman temple at Uppilipalayam in Coimbatore whose annual April car festival is among the larger religious gatherings of the Kongu region.
story: The goddess is said to have cured the soldiers of a Kongu Nadu ruler of chicken pox.

name: Papanasanathar Temple, Papanasam
deity: Shiva as Papanasanathar, with Parvati as Ulagammai
significance: A three-precinct Shiva temple at the foot of the Western Ghats in Tirunelveli district, founded by the Pandya king Chandrakula and enlarged by Vijayanagara and Nayak rulers in the 16th century, with a seven-tiered gateway tower within granite walls; it is run by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Endowment Board.
story: Sage Agastya, unable to reach Kailash for Shiva's wedding, is said to have been granted the sight here, Shiva appearing before him and Lopamudra in the marriage posture.

name: Penneswaraar Temple
significance: Built in 1188 by Kulottunga Chola III after his victory over the Hoysalas, this Krishnagiri-district Shiva temple carries the district's tallest rajagopuram, some forty-two inscribed stones from successive dynasties, and the largest concentration of Navakandam sculptures in Tamil Nadu.
story: Parashurama is said to have prayed to Shiva at Penneswaramadam after destroying the wicked Kshatriyas twenty-one times.

name: Vyagrapurisvarar Temple, Thiruvengaivasal
significance: A Shiva temple in Pudukkottai district whose sanctum faces west so that the evening sun falls on the deity, and which holds an unusual octagonal prakara shrine for Murugan alongside several subsidiary shrines.
story: Guided by the sage Kapila, the divine cow Kamadhenu is said to have worshipped Shiva here by pouring water from her ears and won his blessing.

name: Peddintlamma Temple, Kolletikota
significance: A 13th-century shrine on the shore of Kolleru Lake, raised by an Eastern Ganga army general in the reign of Narasingha Deva I and built in a Kalinga idiom mixed with southern design; it remains a local pilgrimage centre.
story: The general is said to have sacrificed his daughter to win a battle against a rival encampment at Kolleru, and to have built the temple over her memory when the victory came.

name: Bohra Ganesh Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple about two kilometres from central Udaipur, its east-facing image shown dancing; the name records a local practice of leaving written requests for money before the deity, the Bohra community having been the town's traditional moneylenders.

name: Raviswarapuram Siva Temple
significance: An east-facing Shiva temple at Kodungallur counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, recorded in Sangam literature as one of the major temples of the Chera realm; Maha Shivaratri is its main festival.
story: Local tradition holds that the sage Parashurama installed the image here.

name: Varadaraja Perumal Temple, Shoolagiri
deity: Prasanna Varadaraja Perumal (Vishnu), with Perundevi Mahalakshmi
builtDisplay: Chola sanctum; mandapa added by Krishnadevaraya (16th c.)
significance: A Vishnu temple at Shoolagiri in Krishnagiri district whose inner sanctum dates to Chola rule and whose front mandapa was added by Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara, with later contributions from Hoysala rulers and local palayakkarars.
story: The Pandavas are said to have halted here during their forest exile, Arjuna consecrating Varadaraja Perumal, with five great boulders marking their stay.

name: Valiya Koonambaikulam Temple
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; described as very ancient
significance: One of Kerala's older Bhadrakali temples, at Vadakkevila in Kollam, whose Kumbha Bharani festival draws thousands of women for the Chandra Pongal offering; the temple trust also runs an engineering college in the district.

name: Hasanamba Temple
significance: The tutelary goddess temple of Hassan, which takes its name from her, built by the local chieftain Sanjeeva Krishnappa Nayaka in Hoysala times; it is opened only once a year around Deepavali, a ghee lamp left burning inside for the months it stays shut.
story: Seven Matrikas are said to have travelled from Varanasi and stayed on for the beauty of the place, three of them — Maheshwari, Kaumari and Vaishnavi — dwelling in the anthills within the temple.

name: Badrakali Amman Temple, Sivakasi
deity: Badrakali Amman (Bhadrakali, fierce form of Parvati)
significance: The principal temple of Sivakasi, with a five-tiered gopuram some 110 feet high and a gold-plated vimana over the north-facing sanctum; its ten-day Panguni and Chithirai Pongal festivals are the town's largest, and the temple figures in accounts of the 1899 Sivakasi riots.

name: Tadkeshwar Mahadev Temple
builtDisplay: traditionally found in 1215; over 800 years old
significance: A Shiva temple on the bank of the Wanki river near Abrama in Valsad district, remarkable for a roof left deliberately open with a hole about 22 feet across so that the midday sun falls on the six-to-eight-foot semicircular lingam; fairs are held at Maha Shivaratri and through Shravan.
story: The ceiling is said to have been raised twice and lost twice, to fire and then collapse, until Shiva appeared in a devotee's dream saying 'I am Tadkeshwar Mahadev, I need the rays of the sun' — and the temple was left open to the sky.

name: Parumala Valiya Panayannarkavu Devi Temple
deity: Bhadrakali (with the Sapta Matrikas) and Shiva
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; described as very ancient
significance: Set on an island in the Pamba at Parumala, this is reckoned one of the three foremost Bhadrakali temples of Kerala and also counts among the 108 Shiva temples of the state; it is referred to in classical Malayalam literature.
story: Tradition holds that Parashurama installed the Shiva image here, and that the sages Durvasa and Narada installed the goddess in the Treta Yuga.

name: Mundayur Mahadeva Temple
significance: An east-facing Shiva temple at Anjur in Thrissur district, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala; the Zamorin of Kozhikode's army is recorded as having meditated on Shiva here before going into battle. Laksharchana and Shivaratri are its main observances.
story: The image is said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Valisvarar Temple, Sevur
deity: Shiva as Valisvarar, with Aram Valartha Nayaki
significance: A Shiva temple at Sevur in Tiruppur district, counted among the Vaippu Sthalams — shrines named in the hymns of the Tamil Saiva saints Sambandar and Sundarar; Maha Shivaratri is its main festival.
story: The site is said to have been worshipped by Vali of the Ramayana, from whom the deity takes his name.

name: Trilinga Sanghameshwara Temple
deity: Sanghameshwara Swamy (Shiva) with Parvati; three lingams
significance: A Kakatiya-period temple at Vilasagar near Vemulawada raised under Prola II, with three lingams in separate sanctums facing east, north and south beneath stepped pyramidal shikharas; it is treated as a HariHara kshetram, serving both Shaiva and Vaishnava worship.

name: Amunthirathu Devi Temple
builtDisplay: temple built 1988; worship at the site far older
style: Pandya kovil blended with Kerala tradition
significance: A Bhadrakali temple at Mudakkal north of Attingal, holding a black stone image of Amunthirathamma; the community's presence here traces to 1727, when Marthanda Varma brought Vanjipuzha madam Brahmin families from Chengannur to Thiruvananthapuram, and the present temple was built in 1988 and registered as a trust in 2005.

name: Shri Keshavraiji Temple, Bet Dwarka
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; temple registers run back some 250 years
significance: A Krishna temple on Bet Dwarka island beside the Shankh Sarovar tank, built and maintained by the Pushkarna Brahmin community, whose ishtadeva he is; its handwritten registers of visiting devotees go back roughly 250 years.

name: Makaliyam Sreeramaswamy Temple
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; attributed to the Cheras
significance: A Rama temple at Irumpanam near Kochi, attributed to Chera patronage, where Rama is venerated in his form after the slaying of Khara; largely destroyed by fire, it was rebuilt by devotees with copper-plated roofs and panchaloha Dashavatara panels and is now run by the Cochin Devaswom Board.

name: Perumparampu Sri Mahadeva Temple
significance: A centuries-old Shiva temple near Edappal in Malappuram district, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, with a west-facing sanctum of the square Kukkudakruthy form; it was rebuilt in 2010 and keeps Maha Shivaratri as its chief festival.
story: The lingam is said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Krimchi Temples
deity: Shiva, Vishnu, Ganesha and Parvati (group of shrines)
significance: A group of stone temples about 12 km from Udhampur, dated by the Archaeological Survey of India to the 8th–9th centuries and built in the Nagara idiom with rekha shikharas, panchratha plans, gavaksha ornament and pillared mandapas — among the oldest surviving temple architecture in the Jammu region.
story: Locally the group is called the Pandava Temples: Raja Kichak is said to have founded the town, and the Pandavas to have stayed here at length during their exile.

name: Ratangarh Mata Temple
significance: A goddess shrine in the forests of Datia district in Bundelkhand that draws very large Navratri crowds; a stampede on the approach during the 2013 festival killed 115 people and injured more than a hundred.
story: Local tradition holds that Samarth Ramdas, guru of Shivaji, camped here in 1666 to plan the Maratha king's escape from Agra Fort, and that Shivaji was sheltered in this jungle afterwards.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Tithal
builtDisplay: begun 1991 (BAPS); inaugurated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj
significance: A BAPS Swaminarayan mandir standing directly on the beach at Tithal in Valsad district, begun in 1991 and inaugurated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, with carved images of Swaminarayan alongside Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha, Krishna and Hanuman; it has become a fixture of visits to the beach.

name: Kalinka Temple
builtDisplay: present structure c. 2010; shrine centuries old
significance: A Kali shrine on a 2,090 m ridge in the Bironkhal block of Pauri Garhwal, rebuilt around 2010 with a lotus-bud shikhara and run by the Garhwal-Almora Kali Mandir Vikas Samiti, a cooperative of about a dozen surrounding villages.
story: A Badiyaari shepherd is said to have been told in a vision to raise a shrine, and to have piled up rocks into a mound on the mountain top.

name: Karkodeswarar Temple, Kamarasavalli
significance: A Shiva temple at Kamarasavalli near Thirumanur in Ariyalur district, with an east-facing sanctum, a south-facing shrine for Balambika, and the usual rajagopura, prakaram, vimana and kosta niches.
story: The serpent Karkotaka is shown in sculpture worshipping Shiva here with Vinayaka and Nandi, and those born under the sign of Cancer are said to find relief by praying at this shrine.

name: Puramundekkadu Shri Mahadeva Temple
significance: An east-facing Shiva temple at Vattamkulam near Edappal, counted both among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and among the five Shiva temples ringing Guruvayoor; Maha Shivaratri is its main festival.
story: The image is said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Karni Mata Temple, Udaipur
significance: A hilltop shrine holding a stone image of Karni Mata on the Machla Magra ridge above Doodh Talai in Udaipur, reached on foot or by ropeway and known for its outlook over the city and its lakes.

name: Abaya Hastha Swayambu Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Agaram
significance: A Narasimha temple near Hosur built around a swayambhu stone identified in 1998 during land development and still being extended; the land was made over to the Ahobila Mutt, and Narasimha Jayanti is the principal festival.
story: The shrine recalls Vishnu bursting from the pillar as Narasimha, pleased by the devotion of Prahlada.

name: Kanipura Sri Gopalakrishna Temple
builtDisplay: ancient; renovated 10th c. under Kadamba king Jayasimha
significance: An old Vaishnava temple at Kumbla in Kasaragod district holding a jet-black granite Balagopalakrishna, renovated in the 10th century by the Kadamba king Jayasimha whose capital was Kumbla; it is reckoned an Abhimana Kshetram.
story: Krishna is said to have given the image to the sage Kanva in the Dvapara Yuga; the water that flowed from the sage's rites became the Kumbha Hole river, and the town grew around it.

name: Ayyappan Temple, Coimbatore
significance: An Ayyappan temple at Siddhapudur in Coimbatore, planned from 1942 and consecrated in 1969, where worship follows Sabarimala usage; its gold-covered dhwaja stambha, raised in 1972, is described as the only one of its kind in Tamil Nadu.

name: Andoor Kandan Sree Dharma Sastha Temple, Tholady
builtDisplay: rebuilt 2002; grew from the older Tholadichan Kovil
significance: A Dharma Sastha temple at Tholady east of Neyyattinkara, grown out of a small shrine called Tholadichan Kovil and rebuilt in 2002 with new structures and images; Makaravilakku Mahotsavam on 14 January is its main festival.
story: Travellers on the old Tholady path are said to have cut branches and beaten sticks beside the Ayyappa image, and the place took its name from the practice.

name: Kattakampal Temple
significance: A two-acre west-facing temple complex near Kunnamkulam with an east-facing Shiva sanctum and a separate west-facing sanctum for Kattakampal Bhagavathy; it is counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, and the seven-day Kattakampal Pooram in Medam is its great festival.
story: Tradition credits the sage Parashurama with installing the Shiva here, and the festival's high point re-enacts Kali's war with Darika and the demon's killing.

name: Madhava Perumal Temple, Mylapore
significance: A Sri Vaishnava temple in Mylapore, rectangular within ten-foot walls and entered by a five-tier gopuram, held to be the birthplace of Peyalvar, one of the twelve Alvar poet-saints.
story: At the churning of the ocean of milk Vishnu is said to have sent Lakshmi to the hermitage of sage Bhrigu, and to have married his daughter Amritavalli here — whence his other name, Kalyana Perumal.

name: Shree Dev Vyadeshwar Temple
significance: The Shiva temple of Guhagar on the Konkan coast, kuladevata of many Chitpavan families, laid out on the panchayatana plan with the central Shiva shrine ringed by shrines to Surya, Ganesha, Ambika and Vishnu with Lakshmi; three of the shrines were renewed and the east gate restored in 2015.
story: The sage Vyadi is said to have installed the lingam here, and Parashurama — who had raised the Konkan from the sea and settled sixty rishis on it — asked Shiva to meet him daily at the spot, so the god took the name Vyadeshwar, lord of Vyadi.

name: Manikandeswaram Uma Maheswara Temple
deity: Shiva and Parvati (Uma Maheswara), sharing one sanctum
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; traditionally over 2,000 years old
significance: A Kerala-style temple at Vadakkekad unusual for housing Shiva and Parvati together in a single sanctum with Ganesha outside; it was attacked in 1790 by Tipu Sultan, who broke sculptures and carried off its valuables, and though land reform cut its holdings from some 800 acres it remains in daily worship under the Malabar Devaswom Board. The poet Vallathol Narayana Menon wrote parts of his work beneath its banyan tree.

name: Moole Shankareshvara Temple, Turuvekere
style: Bhumija Nagara on a semi-stellate base
significance: A soapstone Shiva temple at Turuvekere built about 1260 under the Hoysala king Narasimha III; Adam Hardy classes its tower as Bhumija Nagara raised on a semi-stellate base, joined to the usual Hoysala sanctum, vestibule and closed hall. It is a protected monument under the Karnataka state archaeology division.

name: Tirttapaleeswarar Temple, Triplicane
significance: A Shiva temple on Natesan Street off the Mylapore–Triplicane road in Chennai, counted among the Sapta Sthana — the seven Shiva temples of Mylapore visited together as a set.

name: Peravallur Sundararaja Perumal Temple
significance: A Vishnu temple in the Peravallur neighbourhood of north Chennai, also known after nearby Periyar Nagar, administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department; Vaikuntha Ekadashi is its principal festival.

name: Arangulanathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thiruvarangulam in Pudukkottai district with a hundred-pillared mandapa and shrines for the three principal Nayanars and all sixty-three; it is one of the Tevaram Vaippu Sthalams named in a hymn of Sambandar.
